sources.citation: Dryer, Matthew S. web pages (acsu.buffalo.edu/~dryer/, papuan.htm), checked 2026-09-17.
sources.note: No Torricelli classification ms or Yambes material posted; only Walman papers.

sources.citation: OLAC: resources in and about the Yambes language (ymb), snapshot 2024-06-24 via Wayback Machine.
sources.note: Catalog lists only Rosetta Swadesh list, Glottolog entry, Ethnologue entry; no SIL archive descriptions, no OPD, no survey report for ymb.

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. Yambes Swadesh List. archive.org item rosettaproject_ymb_swadesh-1 (uploaded 2010).
sources.note: Wordlist only; transcriptions carry no stress marks; no source attribution.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Yambes language' (read 2026-09-17); cites Dryer, Matthew S. 2024, Towards a genealogical classification of Torricelli languages (unpublished ms.) and Drinfeld, Andrey 2024, A Grammar of Aro (University at Buffalo PhD).
sources.note: No phonology content; only classification (Dryer 2024 places Yambes with Kombioic).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 767-780. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. The phylum-wide phonology paragraph (p.769) lists three places of articulation, no voicing contrast, 5-8 vowels, many fricatives; no mention of stress or accent. Yambes appears only in the classification table (Kombio Family, 860 speakers, p.773).

sources.citation: Farr (Henry), Joan. 1992. Kombio Grammar Essentials. Ms., SIL-PNG, 123pp.; Yi, Eunkyung. 2008. Kombio grammar sketch. SIL-PNG.

sources.note: Descriptions of the sister language Kombio (komb1272), the nearest relative with any phonology on record; usable only as a labeled proxy, not as a Yambes statement.

sources.citation: Drinfeld, Andrey. 2024. A Grammar of Aro, a Torricelli language of Papua New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University at Buffalo.

sources.note: Grammar of the closest described Kombioic relative; may include comparative remarks on Yambes and a stress description for the subgroup (proxy only; Aro = torr1259).

sources.citation: Dryer, Matthew S. 2024. Towards a genealogical classification of Torricelli languages. Unpublished manuscript, University at Buffalo.

sources.note: Dryer collected his own field data on Kombio-Yambes languages; the ms (cited by Wikipedia and Drinfeld) is the only modern work known to treat Yambes data and may contain phonological notes including stress.
